hypothesis: The long serial token loop and too few context splits explain much of the observed v1 latency. More splits may improve all storage paths; this alone is not ASTC-specific novelty.
correctness: Unchanged v1 relative-L2 <=1e-4 on each path's own reconstructed values, plus existing engineering decode gate
scope: T384 is the original fixture; T2048/T8192 repeat its known blocks and FP16 K solely as traffic/shape controls, not long-context model quality. All tests repeatedly read one cache and may fit GPU cache.
negative_outcome: Reducing tile length gives no reproducible latency reduction, or an optimized ASTC path remains slower than the best own buffer path. No inference claim from microbenchmarks.
decision: Freeze split choices for each shape before subsequent v2 attribution controls; retain all raw rounds and both session medians. Do not compare batched GPU timings to Python host latency.
